cases.title: Case-insensitive matching applies only under {name:lower}
cases.given: feature/PROJ-1-s-001, m-1-e2e-api, run-2, mixed-case prefix, sdlc/{name:lower}-wip with -WIP
cases.when: branches.py parse runs as a child process in a scratch git repo with a controlled environment
cases.then: Lower format classifies lowercase tails; plain format gives null for s-001 and m-1-e2e-api and RUN-2. run-2 is lowercase in the table, so it classifies under both formats.
cases.expected: Lower format classifies lowercase tails; plain format gives null for s-001 and m-1-e2e-api and RUN-2. run-2 is lowercase in the table, so it classifies under both formats.
cases.actual: Matched. Plan note says run-2 gives null under the plain format; the spec regex ^run-(\d+)$ matches it, so the note is wrong, not the product.

seeds.title: plan note for VS-4 is wrong about run-2
seeds.detail: The plan says run-2 gives null under the plain format. Row 1 is the lowercase literal run-, so it matches under both formats. No product defect.

seeds.title: a branch starting with a dash cannot pass as '--branch -x'
seeds.detail: argparse reads '--branch -wip' as a flag and exits 2 with ok:false. The '--branch=-wip' form works. Git refuses branch names that start with a dash, so this is cosmetic.

seeds.title: slice row accepts any S- tail, such as S-001-attempt-
seeds.detail: Row 8 is ^(S-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)$ as in the spec. A tail like S-001-v-x-0 or S-001-attempt- classifies as a slice with that whole text as id. The spec allows it; the loop may treat such a branch as a loop slice branch.
